_doc: Regional forms (wave 42). {species id: {form id: {name (the suffix: 'Spikkin (Shetland)'), regions [zone regions], zones [optional zone ids that narrow the regions], types [optional replacement types, one change at most], stat_lean {stat: delta, net zero, +/-6}, knack (optional knack id), move (optional signature move id), look {palette {hue, sat, val, tint, tint_amount}, features [crest, ears, speckle, belly, stripe]}, fact}}}. Contract and rules: core/forms.gd. A form of an evolving line should be authored for each stage that spawns it (and the baby stage, so breeding can pass it down) under the same form id.

irish.name: Irish
irish.fact: The Irish hare is a subspecies of the mountain hare found nowhere else, and unlike its Scottish cousin it mostly keeps a brown coat through the winter.

irish.name: Irish
irish.fact: The Irish stoat is its own subspecies, and its winter coat seldom turns fully white.

shetland.name: Shetland
shetland.fact: Shetland sheep are a small, hardy breed that come in a wide range of natural colours and markings.

hebridean.name: Hebridean
hebridean.fact: Hebridean sheep are a small, dark, hardy breed, and many carry two or four horns.

guernsey.name: Guernsey
guernsey.fact: Guernsey cattle are golden-fawn, and their milk is a rich golden colour too, thanks to the carotene in the grass.

bermuda.name: Bermuda
bermuda.fact: Bermuda's only native land reptile is the Bermuda skink, which lives nowhere else on Earth.
